selection: Versioned authored occurrences and explicit legacy migration, selected by the user yes apply it on 2026-09-09.
body: Exactly description and typed_contract. This contract models occurrence identity and graph closure, not typed callable signatures.
steps: An ordered nonempty array of closed step_id and operation_ref objects. Step IDs are unique kebab-case identities; operation_ref is a qualified feature:node selector. Repeated Operation references are permitted and are not duplicate steps.
compensations: A closed array of compensation_id, for_step, operation_ref and depends_on objects. Each compensation has its own unique identity, addresses exactly one declared step, and references an Operation. At most one compensation per step; repeated compensation Operations are permitted. depends_on names other compensation IDs and forms an acyclic graph. An absent compensation is represented by no row, not a magic none Operation.
identity_spaces: Step and compensation IDs are separate owner-local spaces. Qualified Operation identity is a domain concept, neither a step nor a compensation occurrence.
relationships: The exact set of outgoing canonical orchestrates targets equals the distinct qualified Operation references across steps and compensations. Canonical edges are not duplicated for repeated occurrences; unknown targets, non-Operations, missing and surplus edges reject.
ordering: Step array order is retained. Compensation declaration order is not execution order; only declared depends_on edges constrain recovery. No implicit reverse order, retries, parallelism, recovery policy or operation execution is introduced.
migration: A pure helper consumes a registered unchanged legacy graph and explicitly supplied ontology_workflow, step_ids and aligned compensation_ids. Existing checked graph edges resolve qualified Operation references without guessing. It returns a source-bound candidate body and does not modify files. Existing compensation dependencies are translated to the explicitly selected compensation IDs. Candidate materialization must pass normal graph validation.
compatibility: Legacy Workflow parsing, generation and runtime behavior remain separate and unchanged. Existing generators, runtime and formalization explicitly reject the new occurrence version until their own support is implemented.
